title: A to-do list
description:
Write a to-do list manager that reads commands, one per line, until `quit` or the end of the input:

```
add high Buy milk
add Write report
add low Water plants
done 2
list
stats
```

prints

```
Added #1: Buy milk
Added #2: Write report
Added #3: Water plants
Completed #2
[ ] #1 (high) Buy milk
[ ] #3 (low) Water plants
[x] #2 (normal) Write report
3 tasks: 1 done, 2 open (1 high)
```

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `add [high\|low] <text>` | Adds a task with that priority (`normal` when the second word is not `high` or `low`); ids count from 1 and are never reused. Prints `Added #<id>: <text>` |
| `done <id>` | `Completed #<id>`, or `#<id> is already done` |
| `undo <id>` | `Reopened #<id>`, or `#<id> is not done` |
| `remove <id>` | `Removed #<id>` |
| `list` | Open tasks first, by priority (high, normal, low) then id, as `[ ] #<id> (<priority>) <text>`; then done tasks by id as `[x] ...`; or `Nothing to do.` when there are no tasks |
| `stats` | `<n> tasks: <d> done, <o> open (<h> high)`, where high counts open high-priority tasks |
| `quit` | Stops |

Errors: an id that is not a number prints `Not a number: <text>`; an unknown id prints `No task #<id>`; a missing argument prints `Usage: <command> <id>` (or `Usage: add [high|low] <text>`); anything else prints `Unknown command: <word>`. Command words ignore case; blank lines are skipped.
hints: `#[derive(PartialOrd, Ord)]` on an enum orders the variants in the order they are written, so listing `High` first makes it sort first; `sort_by_key(|t| (t.priority, t.id))` sorts by priority, then id.

Make the list's methods return `Result<String, String>` (the message to print either way): `Ok(text)` on success, `Err(text)` on failure, the same `Ok`/`Err` you matched on in lesson 1.05 (lesson 3.04 covers `Result` fully). Then `main` ends with one `match` that prints the text from `Ok` or `Err`.

`self.tasks.remove(index)` takes the item at `index` out of the vector and shifts the later ones down; `for (index, task) in self.tasks.iter().enumerate()` finds the index. Match the command word as a `&str`: `let command: &str = &command_text;`.
requirements: A `Task` struct and a `Priority` enum (derive `PartialOrd`/`Ord` so that sorting puts `High` first).
A `TodoList` struct with methods (`add`, `complete`, `reopen`, `remove`, `find_mut`...) that return `Result<..., String>` or `Option`, and a `main` that only parses lines and prints.
stretch: Add `edit <id> <text>` and a `due <id> <yyyy-mm-dd>` field, listing overdue tasks first.

examples.name: mistakes and edge cases
examples.stdin:
list
add
add high
done
done x
done 7
add low   Call   Ada
done 1
done 1
undo 1
undo 1
remove 1
remove 1
add high High is the text
fly away
LIST
stats
examples.expected:
Nothing to do.
Usage: add [high|low] <text>
Usage: add [high|low] <text>
Usage: done <id>
Not a number: x
No task #7
Added #1: Call Ada
Completed #1
#1 is already done
Reopened #1
#1 is not done
Removed #1
No task #1
Added #2: High is the text
Unknown command: fly
[ ] #2 (high) High is the text
1 tasks: 0 done, 1 open (1 high)
